newsitem.title: UK: Oil slips as Iraq Gulf exports set sail.
newsitem.headline: Oil slips as Iraq Gulf exports set sail.

text.p: Iraq's first oil exports through the Middle East Gulf for six years stopped oil prices rising further on Wednesday, but low oil inventories in key western markets would prevent a price slump for some time yet, oil traders said.
London February futures for benchmark North Sea Brent blend at 1620 GMT were down 42 cents at $23.28 a barrel, shaving some of the dollar-plus gains posted on Monday.
Brent, at an average of $20.20 so far this year, is running $3.30 a barrel higher than its average in 1996.
Supertanker Star Africa sailed late on Tuesday from Iraqi outlet Mina al-Bakr on the Gulf under a United Nations oil-for-food deal.
A second tanker, the Leonidas, has completed loading Iraqi crude and is expected to leave al-Bakr when documentation is complete.
Iraq is allowed to export $2 billion of its oil over six months for humanitarian supplies after six years of international sanctions following its invasion of Kuwait.
Fourteen countries already have confirmed signing contracts with Iraq for almost 400,000 barrels a day (bpd) of sales.
Turkey took the first crude earlier this week from its Ceyhan pipeline with Iraq to the Mediterranean.
Analysts said oil markets would have little difficulty handling the extra Iraqi crude for the time being.

"We do not expect Iraq's return to have a significant downward impact on oil prices in the very short-term since the market is likely to absorb the country's additional exports during the winter months," said finance house Kleinwort Benson in a report.
Latest weekly United States inventory statistics underlined how vunerable stocks are going into the peak period of winter demand.
The U.S. Energy Information Agency on Wednesday reported a 400,000 barrel draw on heating oil and diesel stocks last week, despite an increase in refinery output in most areas of the country.
The prospect of colder weather in key oil-consuming regions in north America this coming weekend has helped prop up prices, dealers said.
